claim: If you use Amazon S3 to serve static content on the internet, AWS recommends using CloudFront to protect the bucket: access to the bucket is restricted so that it's not publicly accessible, end users get lower latency from edge locations closer to them, and requests to S3 origins cost less because data transfer from S3 to CloudFront is free.

evidence.quote: Restricts access to the Amazon S3 bucket so that it's not publicly accessible.
Lower latency for end users by serving content from edge locations closer to them.
Reduced cost for requests to S3 origins (data transfer from S3 to CloudFront is free).
